p: was a certain man in Caesarea: Peter consecrates the first fruits of the Gentiles to God by the means of two miracles.
devout man: So that he worshipped one God, and was not an idolater, and neither could he be void of faith in Christ, because he was a devout man: but as of yet he did not know that Christ had come.
all his house: This is a commendable thing about the man, that he laboured to have all his household, and well-known friends, and acquaintances to be religious and godly.
What is it: What do you want with me Lord? For he prepares himself to hear.

come up for: This is a borrowed kind of speech which the Hebrews used very much, taken from sacrifices and applied to prayers: for it is said of whole burnt sacrifices that the smoke and smell of them goes up into God's nostrils, and so do our prayers, as a sweet smelling sacrifice which the Lord takes great pleasure in.

a memorial before God: That is, in as much that they will not allow God as it were to forget you: for so the Scripture often talks childish with us as nurses do with little children, when they prepare their tongues to speak.

trance: For though Peter does not stand amazed as one that is tongue tied, but talks with God and is instructed in his mysteries, yet his mind was far from being as it normally was; shortly, however, it returned to its normal state.
four corners: So that it seemed to be a square sheet.
all manner of: Here is this word "all" which is general, plainly used for something indefinite and uncertain, that is to say, for some of all sorts, not for all of every sort.
fourfooted beasts of the earth: That is, such as were proper for men's use.
creeping things: To see what is meant by these creeping things see Le 11:2-47.
But Peter said: Peter learns daily in the knowledge of the benefit of Christ, yea, even after he had received the Holy Spirit.
call not thou common: Do not consider them to be unprofitable.
And as Peter was coming in: Religious adoration of worship is proper only to God: but civil worship is given to the ministers of the word, although not without danger.
this hour: He does not mean the very hour at the present time (as it was nine o'clock when he spoke to Peter), but the like, that is, about nine o'clock the other day.
And said: Cornelius' faith demonstrated itself by prayer and charity.
Send therefore to Joppa: As faith comes by hearing, so it is nourished and grows up by the same.

Then Peter opened his mouth: Distinction of nations is taken away by the coming of Christ: and it is evidently seen by their faith and righteousness, which ones are agreeable to him and which ones he accepts.
God is no respecter of persons: That God does not judge according to the outward appearance.

feareth him: By the "fear of God" the Hebrews understood the whole service of God, by which we perceive that Cornelius was not void of faith, no more than they were who lived before Christ's time: and therefore they deal incorrectly who deduce meritorious works and free will from this passage.

word which God sent unto the: God showed the Israelites that whoever lives godly is acceptable to God, no matter what nation he comes from, for he preached peace to men through Jesus Christ, who is Lord not only of one nation, that is, of the Jews, but of all.

That word: The sum of the Gospel (which will be made manifest at the latter day, when Christ himself will sit as judge both of the living and the dead), is this, that Christ promised to the fathers and exhibited in his time with the mighty power of God (which was demonstrated by all means) and at length crucified to reconcile us to God, did rise again the third day, so that whoever believes in him should be saved through the remission of sins.

anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the: This manner of speaking is taken from an old custom of the Jews, who used to anoint their kings and priests, because of which it came to pass to call those anointed upon whom God bestowed gifts and virtues.

chosen before of God: This choosing of the apostles is properly given to God: for though God is president in the lawful election of ministers, yet there is in this place a secret opposition and setting of God's choosing and men's voices against one another, for the apostles are appointed directly by God, and the Church ministers indirectly.
While Peter yet spake these words: The Spirit of God seals that in the heart of the hearers which the minister of the word speaks by the commandment of God, as is evident by the results.
Can any man forbid water: Baptism does not sanctify or make those holy who receive it, but is an outward sign to the world of the profession of faith. (Ed.)
